Energy and carbon footprint of a computation

Source: R/fp.R
co2fp.Rd

Evaluates expr and reports the electricity it used and the CO2-equivalent that electricity implies, by one of two methods, for the grid it ran on, offline. Use it to report the energy and emissions of an analysis next to its results (as journals and funders increasingly ask), or to compare two ways of running the same computation. The result keeps the value of expr, and lists every figure that was assumed rather than measured.

Usage

co2fp(
  expr,
  loc = NULL,
  meth = c("auto", "rapl", "model"),
  cpupwrw = NULL,
  usage = "process",
  loadcur = c("linear", "codecarbon"),
  cores = NULL,
  memgb = NULL,
  mempwrwpergb = 0.3725,
  pue = 1,
  rapldir = "/sys/class/powercap",
  procstat = "/proc/stat",
  devices = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'co2fp'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

expr

The expression to evaluate. It is evaluated once, in the calling environment, when the function reaches it (lazily, as a promise).

loc

The location, passed to co2int. It is a location code, alpha-3 code or name, a number in gCO2e/kWh, or NULL (the default) to detect it.

meth

Character scalar: "auto" (the default; RAPL when readable, else the model), "rapl" (measured; an error when the counters are not readable) or "model" (always the Green Algorithms model).

cpupwrw

The CPU's total thermal design power in watts (the model's \(P_{cpu}\)); NULL uses codecarbon's unknown-CPU fallback.

usage

"process" (measured from this process's CPU time), "machine" (measured from the whole machine's CPU accounting), or a number in between 0 and 1. NULL means "process".

loadcur

Character scalar: "linear" (the default; power proportional to utilisation, as Green Algorithms) or "codecarbon" (codecarbon's curves, see Details). Applies only when cpupwrw is given.

cores

Number of logical cores the process utilisation is measured against; NULL detects it.

memgb

Memory charged to the computation in GB; NULL detects the machine's total memory where it can, else assumes 8 GB.

mempwrwpergb

Memory power per GB (default 0.3725 W/GB, Green Algorithms; codecarbon v2 used 0.375).

pue

Power usage effectiveness: 1 for a laptop or desktop (default); 1.67 is the Green Algorithms default for a data centre, 1.56 the Uptime Institute 2024 global average. Must be a single number of at least 1.

rapldir

Character scalar, the powercap directory holding the RAPL domains; default "/sys/class/powercap" (Linux).

procstat

Character scalar, the kernel CPU accounting file read for usage = "machine"; default "/proc/stat" (Linux).

devices

NULL (the default), or a data frame of the other devices' measured energy, one row per device: kind, vendor, name, watts and/or energy (kWh), and how (see Details).

x

A result of co2fp() or fpeqv().

...

Not used.

Value

A list of class co2fp with elements value (the result of expr), durs (numeric, wall seconds), cputms (numeric, CPU seconds of this process and its children), usage (numeric in \([0, 1]\), the utilisation), usagemode ("process", "machine" or "fixed"), cores (integer), memgb (numeric), enekwh (a list of numerics cpu, memory and total, in kWh, PUE included, and devices when devices is given), co2eg (numeric, grams of CO2-equivalent), co2int (the list returned by co2int, with its year and source), method ("rapl" or "model", the method actually used), assumptions (character vector of every default or fallback that stood in for a measurement) and citations (character vector). With devices, also devices: a data frame with kind, vendor, name, how, kwh (the device's energy before PUE, NA when not counted), counted (logical) and note (how the energy was taken, or why it was not counted). The print method shows a short summary.

Details

Measured (meth = "rapl"): the CPU package energy counters (RAPL, microjoules, read from rapldir) before and after, with wrap-around handled through max_energy_range_uj. This is what codecarbon does on Linux; the counters cover the CPU packages only, so memory is still modelled. Available when raplok() is TRUE.

Modelled (meth = "model"): the Green Algorithms formula (Lannelongue, Grealey and Inouye 2021), $$E = t \,(P_{cpu}\, u + M\, P_{mem})\, PUE$$ with \(t\) the running time, \(P_{cpu}\) the CPU's thermal design power in watts, \(u\) its utilisation, \(M\) the memory in GB, \(P_{mem} = 0.3725\) W/GB and \(PUE\) the data-centre overhead. When the CPU's power is unknown (cpupwrw = NULL) the fallback is codecarbon's: 50\ running time whatever the measured utilisation (the utilisation is still reported, but not applied).

Utilisation is measured, not assumed, in one of two ways. usage = "process" (the default) is this R process's own CPU time, children included, divided by the wall time and the core count: codecarbon's process tracking mode, which charges only what the computation itself used. usage = "machine" is the whole machine's busy share over the run, from /proc/stat on Linux: codecarbon's machine tracking mode, right when the computation is the only thing the machine is doing or when the question is what the machine drew. Where /proc/stat is absent the process figure is used and the assumptions say so. A number between 0 and 1 fixes the utilisation, as the Green Algorithms calculator asks for it. loadcur chooses how power scales with that utilisation: linearly (Green Algorithms) or along codecarbon's curves, a floor at 10\ \(0.1 + 0.9 u^3\) for a machine, so a figure can be made comparable with either tool.

Other devices (devices): the CPU counters and the model cover the CPU and memory only. The energy of a graphics card or another accelerator, measured by its own tools, is added through a table with one row per device and the columns kind (such as "gpu"), vendor, name, watts (the device's average power over the run, in W) and energy (its energy over the run, in kWh) (one of the two may be left out, and a missing value means not measured) and how (how the figure was obtained). A device's energy is its energy, or else watts times the running time; that energy is added to the CPU and memory energy before the PUE and the carbon intensity are applied. A row of kind "cpu" or "memory" is not counted again, nor is a row with neither figure; the result's devices table says which rows were counted and why the others were not. Without devices the result is as described below, with no devices element.

Emissions are \(E \times\) the carbon intensity of the location (co2int: a table compiled into the package of every country at its latest published year and of sub-national zones, so no network access is needed anywhere). With loc = NULL the location is detected from the environment, the time zone or the locale (dtctloc) and the detection is recorded. Every default that stood in for a measurement is listed in assumptions, so a report can say what was measured and what was assumed.

The energy figures include the PUE factor (CPU, memory and total alike). The running time has a floor of the CPU time divided by the cores, so a computation faster than the clock's resolution does not come out at zero. Short computations (well under a second) give figures dominated by timer resolution; measure a representative workload.

Every argument is checked, and the carbon intensity looked up, before expr is evaluated, so a bad argument never costs the computation. Errors: an unknown loc; pue below 1 or not a single finite number; cpupwrw or cores not a single positive number (cores also whole); memgb or mempwrwpergb negative; usage other than "process", "machine" or one number in \([0, 1]\); meth = "rapl" where the counters are not readable; a devices table without its columns or with a negative or infinite figure. An error inside expr propagates unchanged. Nothing is written and nothing is fetched.

References

Lannelongue, L., Grealey, J. and Inouye, M. (2021). Green Algorithms: quantifying the carbon footprint of computation. Advanced Science 8(12), 2100707. doi:10.1002/advs.202100707

Courty, B. et al. (2024). CodeCarbon: estimate and track carbon emissions from machine learning computing. doi:10.5281/zenodo.4658424

Lacoste, A., Luccioni, A., Schmidt, V. and Dandres, T. (2019). Quantifying the carbon emissions of machine learning. arXiv:1910.09700.

See also

co2int, raplok, fpeqv.

Examples

fp <- co2fp(sum(sqrt(seq_len(2e5))), loc = "CA-ON")
fp$enekwh$total
#> [1] 4.026205e-08
fp$co2eg
#> [1] 3.662639e-06
fp$co2int$year
#> [1] 2024
fp$assumptions
#> [1] "CPU power unknown: 85 W x 50% (codecarbon fallback)"
#> [2] "memory charged: the machine's total 15.6 GB"        
print(fp)
#> Computation footprint (modelled)
#>   Time: 0.003 s wall, 0.003 s CPU; utilisation 0.25 (process) on 4 cores
#>   Energy: 4.03e-08 kWh (cpu 3.54e-08, memory 4.85e-09)
#>   CO2e: 3.66e-06 g at 90.97 gCO2e/kWh (Canada, Ontario, 2024)
#>   Assumed: CPU power unknown: 85 W x 50% (codecarbon fallback); memory charged: the machine's total 15.6 GB
# wherever you are, offline: the location is detected and recorded
co2fp(1 + 1, cpupwrw = 45, memgb = 8)$assumptions
#> [1] "location WORLD via fallback, no location found in environment, time zone or locale"
# the whole machine's utilisation, on codecarbon's machine curve
co2fp(
  1 + 1,
  loc = "FR",
  usage = "machine",
  loadcur = "codecarbon",
  cpupwrw = 45,
  memgb = 8
)$usagemode
#> [1] "machine"
# a fixed utilisation and a data-centre PUE, with a carbon intensity given
# as a number
fp2 <- co2fp(
  sum(sqrt(seq_len(2e5))),
  loc = 30,
  usage = 0.5,
  cpupwrw = 65,
  memgb = 16,
  pue = 1.67,
  meth = "model"
)
fp2$enekwh
#> $cpu
#> [1] 4.522917e-08
#> 
#> $memory
#> [1] 8.294333e-09
#> 
#> $total
#> [1] 5.35235e-08
#> 
fpeqv(fp2$co2eg)
#> Footprint in everyday terms
#>   Car travel: 9.175e-09 km
#>   Tree uptake: 1.751e-09 tree-months
# a graphics card measured at 120 W on average (a simulated reading) and
# a CPU row, which is not counted twice
dev <- data.frame(
  kind = c("gpu", "cpu"), vendor = c("example", "example"),
  name = c("card 0", "package 0"), watts = c(120, 35),
  how = c("simulated reading", "simulated reading")
)
fp3 <- co2fp(sum(sqrt(seq_len(2e5))), loc = "CA-ON", cpupwrw = 65,
             memgb = 16, meth = "model", devices = dev)
fp3$devices
#>   kind  vendor      name               how   kwh counted
#> 1  gpu example    card 0 simulated reading 1e-07    TRUE
#> 2  cpu example package 0 simulated reading   NaN   FALSE
#>                                      note
#> 1              average power over the run
#> 2 already counted as CPU or memory energy
# a bad argument is refused before the expression runs
try(co2fp(Sys.sleep(10), pue = 0.9))
#> Error : co2fp: `pue` must be a single number >= 1.
